share_verdict: The batter survived. The oil it fries in did not.

source.text: Vaṭaka is described across the Sanskrit culinary literature, including the Mānasollāsa
source.century: Pre-12th CE, with the Mānasollāsa description 12th CE

ingredients.name: urad dal
ingredients.function: the entire cake. Ground thick, it whips like a batter and holds air, which is what makes a vada light rather than dense

ingredients.name: asafoetida
ingredients.function: digestive; standard with a heavy pulse

ingredients.name: sesame or coconut oil
ingredients.function: the frying medium, a regional, cold-pressed, single-source fat, and the flavour of the dish as much as the batter is

method_reconstructed: Soak and grind the urad dal thick, with almost no water.
Beat the batter by hand until it lightens and a dropped spoonful floats in water.
Work in cracked pepper, ginger and asafoetida.
Shape with a wet palm, thumb through the middle.
Fry in hot oil until it stops bubbling.
contested_points: Vaṭaka names a family of pulse cakes, fried, steamed, and sun-dried keeping-cakes, not exclusively the fried doughnut shape.
Which pulse is intended varies between descriptions; urad is the most common reading but not the only one.

changed.from: regional cold-pressed oil, sesame in the south-east, coconut in the south-west, mustard in the east
changed.driver: solvent extraction and refining produced a cheap neutral oil with a long shelf life and a high smoke point; the regional oils became specialty items
chilli arrived with Portuguese trade and displaced pepper as everyday heat because it grew easily and cost less

ingredients: 2 cups whole urad dal, soaked 4 hours
Cold-pressed sesame or coconut oil for frying
steps: Grind the dal thick, a tablespoon of water at a time, no more. Stop when it is fluffy and pale.
Beat it with your hand or a whisk for three minutes. Drop a bit into water: if it floats, it is ready.
Fold in pepper, ginger, asafoetida and salt.
Wet your palm, flatten a ball, make a hole, slide it into oil at about 170°C.
Fry until the bubbling slows and the colour is deep gold.
The frying medium is not neutral here. A cold-pressed sesame or coconut oil is half of what this tastes like, this is a dish where the fat is an ingredient, not a utility.

verification.note: Seed record. Composite description; not yet checked against a printed edition, so no verse number or page is claimed.
